subject.title: Browser tool should reject or redact URLs with embedded credentials instead of passing them through

question: Should browser page navigation treat HTTP(S) URL-embedded credentials as unsupported input that is rejected and redacted before dispatch?
rationale: The safer default prevents credential leakage, but it intentionally changes behavior for users who may have relied on URL-embedded Basic auth.

options.title: Reject and redact URL userinfo
options.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact diagnostics, and point users to credentials, cookies, headers, or authenticated profiles.

options.title: Support credentialed URLs explicitly
options.body: Keep URL-embedded Basic auth working only if maintainers define a redaction-safe transport contract and tests for every browser path.

options.title: Defer policy and keep current behavior
options.body: Leave the issue open without landing a guard until maintainers decide the compatibility and security tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Reject and redact URL userinfo
recommendation.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact diagnostics, and point users to credentials, cookies, headers, or authenticated profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the strongest history signal around browser plugin ownership and repository security-default policy in the affected area.
